To solve the inequality $f(x)\ge 0,$ we need to find the values of $x$ for which the curve $y=f(x)$ lies above the $x$-axis or touches this axis.

First, we factor the polynomial $f(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+9x \\  & =x({x}^{2}+6x+9) \\  & =x({x}^{2}+3x+3x+9) \\  & =x(x(x+3)+3(x+3)) \\  & =x(x+3)(x+3) \\  & =x(x+3)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The roots of the polynomial $f(x)={x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+9x$ are $x=0$ and $x=-3,$ where

- $x=-3$ has multiplicity $2,$ and

- $x=0$ is a simple root.

So, we can graph the curve as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14007649/assets/24adb4d2477b6db5b51f538f5f3f57c197cbe3d1df53ad1b4e7e9479879f18dd.png)

Since we are interested in solving $f(x)\ge 0,$ we look for the part of the curve that is above the $x$-axis or touches this axis.

Based on the graph, the solution is 

$$
x\in {-3}⋃[0,\infty ).
$$
